function.name: log_rank
function.description: Run Log-Rank test for comparing survival curves between groups. Tests the null hypothesis that the survival functions are equal across groups. Returns chi-squared statistic, p-value, and expected/observed event counts per group.

parameters.description: Request for Log-Rank test comparing survival curves.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

event.description: Name of the column indicating event occurrence (1=event, 0=censored).

group.description: Name of the column defining groups to compare (e.g., 'treatment_group').

time.description: Name of the column containing time-to-event or time-to-censoring values.

function.name: iv_mte
function.description: Estimate Marginal Treatment Effects (MTE) using the Heckman-Vytlacil framework. MTE reveals heterogeneity in treatment effects across the distribution of unobserved resistance to treatment. Returns MTE curve, ATE, ATT, ATU, and LATE estimates. The MTE framework shows how different IV estimands are weighted averages of the MTE curve, providing deeper insight into treatment effect heterogeneity than standard IV/2SLS.

parameters.description:
Request for Marginal Treatment Effects (MTE) estimation.

The MTE framework (Heckman & Vytlacil 2005) connects IV estimation to a
choice-theoretic model of treatment selection, revealing heterogeneity
in treatment effects.

d.description: Name of the binary treatment indicator column (D = 0 or 1).

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

mte_degree.description: Polynomial degree for MTE approximation. Higher degrees allow more flexible MTE shapes but may overfit. Default is 2.

n_grid.description: Number of grid points for evaluating MTE curve. Default is 100.

propensity_model.description: Propensity score model: 'probit' (default), 'logit', or 'linear'. Probit is standard in the MTE literature.

x.description: Optional covariate column names to include in the second stage.

y.description: Name of the outcome variable (Y) column.

z.description: Name of the instrumental variable (Z) column that affects treatment but not outcome directly.

function.name: hypothesis_t_test
function.description: Run Student's t-test for comparing means. Supports: (1) One-sample t-test: compare sample mean to hypothesized value, (2) Two-sample t-test: pass x and y as two numeric columns to compare (Welch's by default), (3) Paired t-test: compare matched pairs. Returns t-statistic, p-value, confidence interval, and effect estimate. Note: x and y must both be numeric columns. To compare a numeric variable across groups (e.g., salary by gender), first filter into two datasets or use two numeric columns.

parameters.description: Request for t-test.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

mu.description: Null hypothesis value (default: 0). For one-sample: hypothesized mean. For two-sample: hypothesized difference.

paired.description: If true, perform a paired t-test. Requires both x and y columns. Default: false.

var_equal.description: For two-sample tests: if true, assume equal variances (Student's t); if false (default), use Welch's t-test.

x.description: Name of the first variable column (must be numeric).

y.description: Name of the second variable column for two-sample or paired tests. Omit for one-sample test.

function.name: list_datasets
function.description: List all currently loaded datasets with their basic information (name, dimensions, column types).

function.name: viz_scatter_interactive
function.description: Generate an interactive scatter plot visualization using Plotly.js. Returns HTML that can be saved to a file and opened in a browser. Supports grouping data by a categorical column for colored traces. Interactive features include zoom, pan, and hover.

parameters.description: Request to generate an interactive scatter plot (HTML/Plotly output).

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

group_column.description: Optional column for grouping data points into separate traces with different colors.

x_column.description: Name of the column for X-axis values.

y_column.description: Name of the column for Y-axis values.

function.name: viz_irf
function.description: Generate an Impulse Response Function (IRF) plot from VAR models. Shows how a variable responds to a shock over time. Optionally includes confidence bands.

parameters.description: Request to generate an IRF (Impulse Response Function) plot.

ci_lower_column.description: Optional column with lower bound of confidence interval.

ci_upper_column.description: Optional column with upper bound of confidence interval.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

response_label.description: Optional label for the response variable.

shock_label.description: Optional label for the shock variable.

function.name: sensemakr
function.description: Run sensitivity analysis for unmeasured confounding (Cinelli & Hazlett 2020). Computes robustness value (RV) - the minimum confounding strength needed to nullify the treatment effect. Key outputs: (1) Partial R²: how much variance treatment explains in outcome, (2) RV_q: confounding needed to reduce effect by q%, (3) RV_alpha: confounding needed to make effect insignificant, (4) Benchmark bounds: adjusted estimates under various confounding scenarios. Essential for causal inference to assess how robust findings are to unmeasured confounding.

parameters.description: Request for sensitivity analysis for unmeasured confounding (sensemakr).

alpha.description: Significance level for robustness value calculation. Default: 0.05.

benchmark_covariates.description: Covariate names to use as benchmarks. Their partial R² provides intuition about confounding magnitude.

contour_data.description: Whether to generate data for sensitivity contour plots. Default: false.

covariates.description: Names of the control covariate columns. These are conditioned on when assessing confounding.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

kd.description: Multiplier applied to benchmark partial R² with treatment. E.g., kd=2 assumes confounder is twice as strong. Default: 1.0.

ky.description: Multiplier applied to benchmark partial R² with outcome. Default: same as kd.

q.description: Proportion of the effect to explain away. q=1 (default) means nullify; q=0.5 means reduce by half.

treatment.description: Name of the treatment variable whose coefficient will be analyzed for sensitivity.

y.description: Name of the outcome variable (Y) column.

function.name: panel_random_effects
function.description: Run Random Effects (GLS) panel regression. Assumes individual effects are uncorrelated with regressors. More efficient than FE if assumption holds.

parameters.description: Request for Panel Random Effects regression.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

x.description: Names of the independent variable (X) columns.

y.description: Name of the dependent variable (Y) column.

function.name: list_cleaning_sessions
function.description: List all active cleaning sessions with their current status.

parameters.description: Request to list all active cleaning sessions.

function.name: natural_effects_mediation
function.description: Perform Natural Effect Models (medflex) mediation analysis that allows for treatment-mediator interactions. Decomposes total effect into Natural Direct Effect (NDE) and Natural Indirect Effect (NIE) using the regression-based approach of Lange, Vansteelandt, & Bekaert (2012). Unlike IPW-based mediation, this method uses regression models for both mediator and outcome, with optional A*M interaction terms. Returns effect estimates, bootstrap CIs, and model diagnostics.

parameters.description: Request for Natural Effect Models (medflex) mediation analysis.

allow_interaction.description: Include treatment-mediator interaction term in outcome model. Default is true. Set to false for simple product-of-coefficients decomposition.

confidence_level.description: Confidence level for intervals (e.g., 0.95 for 95% CI). Default is 0.95.

confounders.description: Names of confounder columns for adjustment in mediator and outcome models. Can be empty.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

mediator.description: Name of the mediator variable column - the intermediate variable through which treatment may affect the outcome.

n_bootstrap.description: Number of bootstrap replications for confidence intervals. Default is 1000. Set to 0 to use delta method instead.

outcome.description: Name of the outcome variable column (continuous).

scale.description: Scale for reporting effects: 'difference' (default for continuous outcomes), 'ratio' (for log-link), 'odds_ratio' (for logit).

treatment.description: Column indicating treatment status (1 = treated, 0 = control). Typically binary.

function.name: timeseries_embed
function.description: Create a lag embedding matrix from a time series. Each row contains consecutive values, useful for building AR models or phase space reconstruction.

parameters.description: Request for time series embedding.

column.description: Name of the time series column to embed.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

dimension.description: Number of columns in the embedding matrix (lag dimension).

function.name: viz_heatmap
function.description: Generate a correlation heatmap visualization for numeric columns. Uses a diverging blue-white-red colormap. Returns a base64-encoded PNG image.

parameters.description: Request to generate a correlation heatmap.

columns.description: Names of numeric columns to include. If not specified, uses all numeric columns.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

function.name: ml_cutree
function.description: Cut a hierarchical clustering dendrogram into groups (cutree). First performs hierarchical clustering, then cuts the resulting tree at a specified number of clusters (k) or height. Returns cluster assignments for each observation. Useful for extracting cluster memberships from a dendrogram.

parameters.description: Request for cutting a hierarchical clustering tree (cutree).

columns.description: Names of the numeric columns to cluster.

cut_height.description: Height (distance threshold) at which to cut the dendrogram. Ignored if k is specified.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

k.description: Number of clusters to cut the tree into. Takes priority over cut_height.

function.name: ml_cmdscale
function.description: Classical Multidimensional Scaling (cmdscale) for embedding distances into Euclidean space. Takes a data matrix and computes a low-dimensional configuration that preserves pairwise Euclidean distances. Returns point coordinates and goodness-of-fit measures. Useful for visualizing similarity/dissimilarity data.

parameters.description: Request for Classical Multidimensional Scaling (cmdscale).

columns.description: Names of the numeric columns to include. Euclidean distances will be computed from these columns.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

is_distance_matrix.description: Set to true if the input columns represent a distance matrix. Default is false (data is converted to distances).

k.description: Number of dimensions in the output configuration. Default is 2.

function.name: munge_deduplicate
function.description: Remove duplicate rows from a dataset. Specify which duplicate to keep: 'first', 'last', or 'none'.

parameters.description: Request to remove duplicate rows.

columns.description: Column names to check for duplicates. If not provided, checks all columns.

dataset.description: Name or ID of the dataset.

keep.description: Which duplicate to keep: 'first', 'last', or 'none'. Default is 'first'.

function.name: synthetic_control
function.description: Run Synthetic Control Method for comparative case studies with a single treated unit. Creates a weighted combination of control (donor) units to construct a synthetic counterfactual. Developed by Abadie, Diamond, and Hainmueller (2010). Returns unit weights, predictor balance, treatment effects at each post-treatment period, and optional placebo-based inference (p-values).

column.description: Column name of the predictor variable.

time_window.description: Time window for predictor aggregation as [start, end]. If omitted, uses all pre-treatment periods.

parameters.description: Request for Synthetic Control Method.

custom_v_weights.description: Custom predictor weights (only used if v_method is 'custom'). Must sum to 1.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded panel dataset.

max_iter.description: Maximum iterations for V optimization. Default is 1000.

optimization_window.description: Time window for optimization [start, end]. If omitted, uses all pre-treatment periods.

outcome.description: Name of the outcome variable column.

predictors.description: List of predictor specifications. Can be column names (strings) or detailed specs with aggregation and time windows.

run_placebos.description: Whether to run placebo tests for inference. Default is false (can be slow with many units).

time_col.description: Name of the column identifying time periods (must be integer, e.g., 'year').

tolerance.description: Tolerance for optimization convergence. Default is 1e-6.

treated_unit.description: Name or ID of the treated unit (must match values in unit_col).

treatment_time.description: First post-treatment period (treatment starts at or after this time).

unit_col.description: Name of the column identifying units (e.g., 'state', 'country').

v_method.description: Method for predictor importance weights: 'datadriven' (default), 'equal', or 'custom'.

weight_threshold.description: Minimum weight to display in output (for readability). Default is 0.001.

function.name: data_quality_profile
function.description: Generate a comprehensive data quality profile for LLM-assisted data cleaning. Returns column-level statistics (nulls, uniques, types), numeric outlier detection, string pattern analysis, and automated issue detection with severity ratings.

parameters.description: Request for data quality profile.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

function.name: linalg_toeplitz
function.description: Construct a Toeplitz matrix - a matrix with constant values along each diagonal. Useful for autocorrelation matrices, circulant matrices, and time series analysis. Can create symmetric or asymmetric Toeplitz matrices.

parameters.description: Request for Toeplitz matrix construction.

column.description: Values for the first column. For a symmetric matrix, this is also the first row.

row.description: Values for the first row. If not specified, creates a symmetric matrix using column values.

function.name: viz_line_interactive
function.description: Generate an interactive line chart visualization using Plotly.js. Returns HTML that can be saved to a file and opened in a browser. Interactive features include zoom, pan, and hover.

parameters.description: Request to generate an interactive line chart (HTML/Plotly output).

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

x_column.description: Name of the column for X-axis values (e.g., time index).

y_column.description: Name of the column for Y-axis values.

function.name: stats_mauchly_test
function.description: Mauchly's test for sphericity in repeated measures designs. Tests whether the variances of the differences between all combinations of conditions are equal. Includes epsilon corrections (Greenhouse-Geisser, Huynh-Feldt). Equivalent to R's mauchly.test().

parameters.description: Request for Mauchly's sphericity test.

columns.description: Names of columns representing repeated measures (at least 3 required).

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

function.name: stats_ecdf
function.description: Compute the empirical cumulative distribution function (ECDF) for a numeric column. Returns step function values at data points or specified evaluation points. Equivalent to R's ecdf().

parameters.description: Request for empirical CDF.

at.description: Optional specific values at which to evaluate the ECDF. If omitted, returns ECDF at all sorted unique data values.

column.description: Name of the numeric column.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

function.name: regression_loess
function.description: Fit a LOESS (LOcally Estimated Scatterplot Smoothing) model. LOESS fits local polynomial regressions at each point, weighted by distance from the target point using tricubic weights. Useful for non-parametric trend estimation, data smoothing, and exploring nonlinear relationships. Returns fitted values, residuals, R-squared, and equivalent number of parameters.

parameters.description: Request for LOESS local regression.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

degree.description: Degree of local polynomial: 1 (linear) or 2 (quadratic, default). Quadratic captures curvature better at boundaries.

robust.description: Use robust fitting with iterative reweighting to downweight outliers. Default: false (gaussian family). Set true for 'symmetric' family.

span.description: Smoothing parameter controlling neighborhood size. Range (0,1] uses proportion of data; >1 uses all points. Default: 0.75. Smaller = more wiggly, larger = smoother.

x.description: Name of the independent variable (X) column.

y.description: Name of the dependent variable (Y) column to smooth.

function.name: ml_hierarchical
function.description: Run Hierarchical clustering using agglomerative approach. Supports Ward, single, complete, and average linkage methods. Returns cluster assignments and dendrogram information.

parameters.description: Request for Hierarchical clustering.

columns.description: Names of the numeric columns to use as features for clustering.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

distance_threshold.description: Distance threshold for cutting. Used if n_clusters is not specified.

n_clusters.description: Number of clusters to create. If not specified, uses distance_threshold.

function.name: anova_one_way
function.description: Run one-way Analysis of Variance (ANOVA) to test whether means differ across groups. Returns F-statistic, p-value, effect sizes (eta-squared, omega-squared), and group statistics. Use when comparing a continuous response variable across 2+ categorical groups.

parameters.description: Request for one-way ANOVA.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

factor.description: Name of the factor (grouping) variable column. Groups observations for comparison.

response.description: Name of the response (dependent) variable column. Must be numeric.

function.name: regression_nls
function.description: Fit a nonlinear regression model using Levenberg-Marquardt algorithm. Supports common models: exponential decay/growth, Michaelis-Menten kinetics, logistic growth, power law, asymptotic. Returns parameter estimates, standard errors, t-values, and convergence info.

parameters.description: Request for nonlinear least squares (NLS).

algorithm.description: Optimization algorithm: 'levenberg_marquardt' (default, more robust) or 'gauss_newton' (faster but may not converge).

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

model.description: Nonlinear model to fit: 'exponential_decay' (y = a*exp(-b*x) + c), 'exponential_growth' (y = a*exp(b*x)), 'michaelis_menten' (y = Vmax*x/(Km+x)), 'logistic' (y = K/(1+exp(-r*(x-x0)))), 'power' (y = a*x^b), 'asymptotic' (y = a - b*exp(-c*x)).

start.description: Initial parameter values. For exponential_decay: [a, b, c]. For exponential_growth: [a, b]. For michaelis_menten: [Vmax, Km]. For logistic: [K, r, x0]. For power: [a, b]. For asymptotic: [a, b, c].

x.description: Name of the independent variable (X) column.

y.description: Name of the dependent variable (Y) column.

function.name: sphet_model
function.description: Run spatial regression via GMM with heteroscedasticity-robust estimation. Implements the Kelejian-Prucha (1998, 1999, 2010) GMM estimator that is robust to heteroscedasticity of unknown form. Supports SAR (lag), SEM (error), and SARAR (combined) models. Unlike ML estimation, GMM does not require normally distributed errors. Returns heteroscedasticity-robust or HAC standard errors. Equivalent to R's sphet::spreg() and sphet::gstslshet().

parameters.description: Request for Spatial GMM with Heteroscedasticity Robustness (sphet).

bandwidth.description: Bandwidth for HAC estimation. If not specified, uses automatic bandwidth selection.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

instrument_order.description: Order of spatial lag instruments [X, WX, W^2X, ...]. Default is 2.

model.description: Model type: 'lag' for SAR (y=lambda*Wy+Xb+e), 'error' for SEM (y=Xb+u, u=rho*Wu+e), or 'sarar' for combined. Default is 'lag'.

se_type.description: Standard error type: 'robust' for heteroscedasticity-robust (Kelejian-Prucha 2010), 'hac' for HAC (Kelejian-Prucha 2007), or 'standard' for homoscedastic. Default is 'robust'.

weights.description: Name of previously created spatial weights (from spatial_neighbors tool).

x.description: Names of the independent variable (X) columns.

y.description: Name of the dependent variable (Y) column.

function.name: treatment_twang
function.description: Estimate propensity scores using Gradient Boosted Machine (GBM) with automatic tuning for covariate balance (twang). Unlike logistic regression, twang uses machine learning and automatically selects the optimal number of iterations based on balance metrics (standardized effect sizes or KS statistics). Particularly useful when you need good balance across many covariates. Returns propensity scores, IPW weights, optimal iteration number, and balance diagnostics before/after weighting.

parameters.description: Request for twang GBM propensity score estimation.

balance_threshold.description: Balance threshold below which to stop early. Default is 0.1.

covariates.description: Names of covariate columns to include in the GBM propensity score model.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

estimand.description: Target estimand: 'att' (effect on treated, default), 'ate' (average treatment effect), 'atc' (effect on control).

n_trees.description: Maximum number of gradient boosting iterations. Default is 3000.

shrinkage.description: Learning rate for gradient boosting. Smaller values need more iterations but often give better results. Default is 0.01.

stop_method.description: Stopping rule for selecting optimal iterations: 'es.mean' (mean standardized effect size, default), 'es.max' (max effect size), 'ks.mean' (mean KS statistic), 'ks.max' (max KS statistic).

treatment.description: Column indicating treatment status (1 = treated, 0 = control). Must be binary.

function.name: heterogeneity_test
function.description: Test for treatment effect heterogeneity using Fisherian randomization inference. Tests H0: all individual treatment effects are equal (tau_i = tau). Returns permutation p-value, estimated individual effects, ATE, and optionally decomposes heterogeneity into systematic (explained by covariates) and idiosyncratic components. Based on R package 'hettx' by Ding, Feller & Miratrix.

parameters.description: Request for Treatment Effect Heterogeneity Test (hettx).

covariates.description: Names of covariate columns for matching and decomposition.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

decompose.description: Whether to decompose heterogeneity into systematic and idiosyncratic components. Default is true.

effect_method.description: Method for estimating individual effects: 'matching' (default), 'regression', or 'stratified'.

n_neighbors.description: Number of nearest neighbors for matching-based imputation. Default is 3.

n_permutations.description: Number of permutations for Fisherian inference. Default is 1000.

outcome.description: Name of the outcome variable (Y).

seed.description: Optional random seed for reproducible results.

treatment.description: Name of the binary treatment indicator (0/1).

function.name: regression_harvtest
function.description: Harvey-Collier test for detecting departure from linearity. Uses recursive residuals to test whether the mean of one-step-ahead forecast errors differs from zero. A significant result suggests convex or concave functional misspecification - the linear model may need polynomial terms. Equivalent to R's lmtest::harvtest().

parameters.description: Request for Harvey-Collier test for linearity.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

x.description: Names of the independent variable (X) columns.

y.description: Name of the dependent variable (Y) column.

function.name: panel_unit_root
function.description: Run panel unit root tests to test for stationarity in panel data. Supports LLC (Levin-Lin-Chu), IPS (Im-Pesaran-Shin), Fisher/Maddala-Wu, and Hadri tests. Panel tests have more power than univariate tests by exploiting cross-sectional variation. LLC assumes common unit root, IPS allows heterogeneous roots, Hadri tests null of stationarity.

parameters.description: Request for Panel Unit Root tests.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded panel dataset.

lags.description: Number of lags for ADF regression. If not specified, uses automatic selection.

model.description: Model specification: 'none' (no deterministic terms), 'constant' (individual intercepts, default), 'trend' (individual intercepts and trends).

time_col.description: Column name for time period identifier (e.g., 'year', 'quarter').

unit_col.description: Column name for panel unit identifier (e.g., 'country', 'firm_id').

variable.description: Name of the variable column to test for unit root.

function.name: collaborative_tmle
function.description: Estimate Average Treatment Effect (ATE) using C-TMLE - extends TMLE with data-adaptive covariate selection for the propensity score model. Uses cross-validation to select which covariates to include, reducing finite-sample bias from including too many covariates while maintaining double robustness. Returns ATE estimate, selected covariates, selection path with CV criterion at each step, and influence curve-based standard errors.

parameters.description: Request for Collaborative Targeted Maximum Likelihood Estimation (C-TMLE).

covariates.description: Names of candidate covariate columns. C-TMLE will select which ones to include in the propensity score model via cross-validation.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

max_covariates.description: Maximum number of covariates to include in propensity score model. Default is no limit.

n_folds.description: Number of cross-validation folds for covariate selection. Default is 5.

outcome.description: Name of the outcome variable column. Can be binary or continuous.

ps_lower.description: Lower bound for propensity score truncation. Default is 0.025.

ps_upper.description: Upper bound for propensity score truncation. Default is 0.975.

q_model.description: Outcome model type: 'logistic' for binary outcomes (default), 'linear' for continuous outcomes.

stopping_rule.description: Stopping rule for selection: 'cv_minimum' (stop at minimum CV risk, default), 'one_se' (one-standard-error rule for parsimony), 'max_covariates' (use max_covariates parameter).

treatment.description: Column indicating treatment status (1 = treated, 0 = control). Must be binary.

function.name: timeseries_pp_test
function.description: Test for unit root in a time series using the Phillips-Perron test. Tests H₀: series has unit root (non-stationary) vs H₁: series is stationary. Uses Newey-West long-run variance estimator with Bartlett weights for serial correlation correction. Similar to ADF test but makes non-parametric correction. Returns: Z(τ) statistic, truncation lag, p-value, and diagnostics.

parameters.description: Request for Phillips-Perron unit root test.

column.description: Name of the numeric time series column to test for unit root.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

lshort.description: Whether to use short truncation lag formula: trunc(4*(n/100)^0.25). If false, uses long formula: trunc(12*(n/100)^0.25). Default: true.

function.name: rd_bw
function.description: Compute MSE-optimal bandwidth for Regression Discontinuity estimation. Returns bandwidth values without running the full estimation. Useful for inspecting bandwidth selection before estimation.

parameters.description: Request for RD bandwidth selection only.

cutoff.description: Cutoff value for the running variable. Default is 0.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

outcome.description: Name of the outcome variable (Y) column.

p.description: Polynomial order for estimation. Default is 1.

running_var.description: Name of the running (forcing) variable (X) column.

function.name: describe_dataset
function.description: Get summary statistics for a loaded dataset including column types, null counts, and basic statistics for numeric columns.

parameters.description: Request to describe a loaded dataset.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

function.name: ml_pca
function.description: Run Principal Component Analysis (PCA) for dimensionality reduction. Returns principal components, explained variance ratios, and loadings. Useful for understanding data structure and reducing feature dimensionality.

parameters.description: Request for PCA (Principal Component Analysis).

columns.description: Names of the numeric columns to include in PCA.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

n_components.description: Number of principal components to keep. If not specified, keeps all components.

function.name: etwfe
function.description: Estimate treatment effects using Extended TWFE (Wooldridge 2021, 2023). Addresses heterogeneous treatment effects in staggered DiD by estimating saturated cohort-by-time interactions. Returns cohort-time ATT estimates, event study by relative time, cohort averages, and overall ATT. Robust to treatment effect heterogeneity across cohorts and over time.

parameters.description: Request for Extended Two-Way Fixed Effects (ETWFE) estimation.

cgroup.description: Control group: 'notyet' (default) uses not-yet-treated units, 'never' uses only never-treated units.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded panel dataset.

first_treat.description: Column indicating when each unit was first treated (period number). Use 0 for never-treated units.

outcome.description: Name of the outcome variable column.

time_col.description: Column containing the time period identifier (e.g., year, quarter).

treatment.description: Column indicating treatment status (1 = currently treated, 0 = not treated). Binary indicator.

unit_col.description: Column containing the unit/individual identifier (e.g., state_id, firm_id).

function.name: ml_c50
function.description: C5.0 Decision Tree for classification (Quinlan's successor to C4.5). Uses information gain ratio for splitting, pessimistic error pruning, and optionally boosting via AdaBoost.M1. Features: automatic feature selection (winnowing), rule extraction, multiclass support. Returns tree structure, rules (if requested), variable importance, and class predictions. Based on R's C50 package.

parameters.description: Request for C5.0 Decision Tree classification.

cf.description: Confidence factor for pessimistic error pruning (0-1). Lower = more pruning. Default is 0.25.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

features.description: Names of the feature columns (X variables).

min_cases.description: Minimum number of cases required in a leaf node. Default is 2.

rules.description: If true, extract rule-based model from tree. Default is false (tree output).

seed.description: Optional random seed for reproducible results.

target.description: Name of the target column (categorical Y variable).

trials.description: Number of boosting iterations. Default is 1 (no boosting). Set > 1 for AdaBoost.M1 ensemble.

winnow.description: If true, perform feature selection to remove uninformative predictors. Default is false.

function.name: timeseries_cpgram
function.description: Cumulative periodogram (cpgram) - diagnostic tool for testing if a time series is white noise. Plots cumulative sum of periodogram ordinates. For white noise, should follow a uniform distribution. Returns cumulative periodogram, confidence bands, and Kolmogorov-Smirnov test for white noise.

parameters.description: Request for cumulative periodogram (cpgram).

column.description: Name of the time series column.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

taper.description: Proportion of data to taper at each end (0.0-0.5). Default is 0.1.

function.name: panel_gmm
function.description: Run Arellano-Bond (difference GMM) or Blundell-Bond (system GMM) estimation for dynamic panel data models. Handles endogeneity of lagged dependent variables using lagged levels/differences as instruments. Reports Sargan test for overidentifying restrictions and AR(1)/AR(2) tests for serial correlation.

parameters.description: Request for Arellano-Bond / System GMM dynamic panel estimation.

collapse.description: Whether to collapse instruments to reduce instrument count. Default: false.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

lags.description: Number of lags of Y to use as regressors. Default: 1.

function.name: ml_tsne
function.description: Run t-SNE (t-distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding) for visualizing high-dimensional data in 2D or 3D. Preserves local structure while revealing clusters. Good for exploratory visualization.

columns.description: Names of the numeric columns to include in t-SNE.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

seed.description: Optional random seed for reproducible results.

function.name: hypothesis_chisq_independence
function.description: Run Pearson's chi-squared test of independence to check if two categorical variables are independent. Creates a contingency table from two columns and tests H₀: row and column variables are independent. For 2×2 tables, Yates' continuity correction is applied by default. Returns chi-squared statistic, p-value, degrees of freedom, expected values, and residuals.

parameters.description: Request for chi-squared test of independence.

col_var.description: Name of the column for columns of the contingency table.

correct.description: If true and table is 2×2, apply Yates' continuity correction. Default: true.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

row_var.description: Name of the column for rows of the contingency table.

function.name: regression_driscoll_kraay
function.description: Compute Driscoll-Kraay (1998) panel-robust standard errors. Robust to arbitrary cross-sectional correlation (spatial dependence) and serial correlation in panel data. Aggregates score vectors by time period and applies Newey-West HAC correction. Best for panels with large T (many time periods). Returns coefficient estimates with panel-robust SEs, t-stats, and p-values.

parameters.description: Request for Driscoll-Kraay panel-robust standard errors.

bandwidth.description: Bandwidth for HAC kernel. Default uses Newey-West rule: floor(T^0.25). Higher values allow for more serial correlation.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded panel dataset.

time_col.description: Column containing time period identifiers (e.g., 'year', 'quarter'). Used to aggregate scores within periods.

x.description: Names of the independent variable (X) columns.

y.description: Name of the dependent variable (Y) column.

function.name: bp_bounds
function.description: Compute Balke-Pearl bounds for nonparametric IV analysis. Provides sharp bounds on the Average Causal Effect (ACE) without parametric assumptions. All three variables (instrument Z, treatment D, outcome Y) must be binary (0/1). Returns bounds with optional bootstrap confidence intervals. Also reports the Wald (standard IV) estimate for comparison. Use monotonicity=true if you can assume no defiers (instrument only affects treatment in one direction).

parameters.description:
Request for Balke-Pearl bounds on the Average Causal Effect (ACE).

Balke-Pearl bounds provide sharp nonparametric bounds on the causal effect
using instrumental variables without assuming parametric models.

bootstrap_ci.description: Whether to compute bootstrap confidence intervals for the bounds. Default is true.

confidence_level.description: Confidence level for intervals. Default is 0.95 (95% CI).

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

instrument.description: Name of the binary instrument column (Z). Example: randomized treatment assignment.

monotonicity.description: Whether to assume monotonicity (no defiers). If true, bounds tighten but assumption may be violated. Default is false.

n_bootstrap.description: Number of bootstrap replications for confidence intervals. Default is 1000.

outcome.description: Name of the binary outcome column (Y). Example: recovery status.

seed.description: Optional random seed for bootstrap reproducibility.

treatment.description: Name of the binary treatment received column (D). Example: actual treatment uptake.

function.name: suggest_cleaning
function.description: Analyze a dataset and generate prioritized cleaning suggestions. Returns specific operations with parameters, estimated impact, and reasoning. Use this to get intelligent recommendations before starting a cleaning workflow.

parameters.description: Request to generate smart cleaning suggestions.

dataset.description: The name/ID of the loaded dataset.

limit.description: Maximum number of suggestions to return. Default: all.

min_priority.description: Minimum priority: 'low', 'medium', 'high', or 'critical'. Default: include all.

function.name: hypothesis_mantelhaen
function.description: Run Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test for conditional independence in stratified 2×2 tables. Tests whether two binary variables are associated while controlling for a third (stratum) variable. Returns CMH chi-squared statistic, p-value, common odds ratio estimate with confidence interval, and per-stratum statistics.

parameters.description: Request for Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test.

col_var.description: Name of the column containing the column variable (must have exactly 2 levels, e.g., 'disease'/'healthy').

correct.description: Whether to apply Yates' continuity correction. Default: true.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

row_var.description: Name of the column containing the row variable (must have exactly 2 levels, e.g., 'exposed'/'unexposed').

stratum_var.description: Name of the column containing stratum identifiers (e.g., 'hospital', 'study_site').

function.name: regression_lasso
function.description: Run lasso regression (L1-penalized linear regression). Shortcut for glmnet with alpha=1. Performs automatic feature selection by shrinking some coefficients to zero.

parameters.description: Request for lasso regression (shortcut for glmnet with alpha=1).

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

lambda.description: Optional sequence of lambda (regularization) values. If omitted, automatically generates a path.

x.description: Names of the independent variable (X) columns.

y.description: Name of the dependent variable (Y) column.

function.name: regression_supsmu
function.description: Friedman's SuperSmoother - a variable-bandwidth smoother that locally adapts to the data. Uses cross-validation to select optimal span at each point. Returns smoothed y values and can handle periodic data.

parameters.description: Request for super smoother (supsmu).

bass.description: Bass parameter controlling smoothness (0-10). Higher = smoother. Default is 0.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

periodic.description: Whether to treat x as periodic on [0, 1]. Default is false.

span.description: Fixed span fraction (0-1). If not specified, cross-validation selects optimal span.

weights.description: Optional name of the weight column.

x.description: Name of the predictor column (X variable).

y.description: Name of the response column (Y variable).

function.name: munge_lag_lead
function.description: Create lag or lead columns for time series or panel data. Lag shifts values forward (past values), lead shifts values backward (future values).

parameters.description: Request to create lag or lead columns.

column.description: Column name to create lag/lead for.

dataset.description: Name or ID of the dataset.

direction.description: Direction: 'lag' (shift forward) or 'lead' (shift backward). Default is 'lag'.

periods.description: Number of periods to shift. Positive for lag, negative for lead (or use 'direction').

function.name: str_regex_extract
function.description: Extract substrings matching a regex pattern into a new column. Use capture groups () to specify what to extract, or extract the whole match.

column.description: Name of the string column to extract from.

new_column.description: Name for the new column containing extracted values.

pattern.description: Regular expression pattern. Use capture groups () to specify what to extract.

function.name: sar_model
function.description: Run Spatial Autoregressive Lag (SAR) model: y = ρWy + Xβ + ε. Estimates spatial lag parameter ρ via maximum likelihood. Use when there is substantive spatial interaction (e.g., neighbors' outcomes affect own outcome). Optionally estimates Spatial Durbin Model (SDM) with spatially lagged covariates. Equivalent to R's spatialreg::lagsarlm().

parameters.description: Request for Spatial Autoregressive (SAR) model.

compute_impacts.description: If true, computes direct, indirect, and total spatial impacts. Default is true.

x.description: Names of the independent variable (X) columns.

y.description: Name of the dependent variable (Y) column.

function.name: timeseries_ar
function.description: Fit an autoregressive model to time series data with automatic order selection via AIC. Supports Yule-Walker (default), Burg, and OLS methods. Returns AR coefficients, prediction variance, AIC values, partial autocorrelations, and residuals.

parameters.description: Request for AR (autoregressive) model fitting.

aic.description: Whether to use AIC for automatic order selection. Default: true.

column.description: Name of the column containing the time series values.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

order.description: Specific AR order to fit. If provided with aic=false, uses this exact order.

order_max.description: Maximum AR order to consider. Default: min(n-1, 10*log10(n)).

function.name: timeseries_structts
function.description: Fit a structural time series model by maximum likelihood using the Kalman filter. Supports: 'level' (local level/random walk + noise, equivalent to ARIMA(0,1,1)), 'trend' (local linear trend, equivalent to ARIMA(0,2,2)), and 'bsm' (basic structural model with level, trend, and seasonality). Returns variance parameters, smoothed components, fitted values, residuals, log-likelihood, AIC, and BIC.

parameters.description: Request for structural time series model fitting.

column.description: Name of the column containing the time series values.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

model_type.description: Type of structural model: 'level' (local level/random walk + noise), 'trend' (local linear trend), or 'bsm' (basic structural model with seasonality).

period.description: Seasonal period for BSM model (e.g., 12 for monthly data with yearly seasonality). Required for 'bsm' type.

function.name: spatial_lm_tests_tool
function.description: Run Lagrange Multiplier tests for spatial dependence. Tests for spatial lag (SAR) vs spatial error (SEM) dependence in OLS residuals. Includes robust versions that account for the presence of the other form of spatial dependence. Use to decide between SAR and SEM models. Equivalent to R's spdep::lm.LMtests().

parameters.description: Request for spatial LM tests.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

weights.description: Name of previously created spatial weights (from spatial_neighbors tool).

x.description: Names of the independent variable (X) columns.

y.description: Name of the dependent variable (Y) column.

function.name: timeseries_acf
function.description: Compute autocorrelation function (ACF), autocovariance, or partial autocorrelation function (PACF) for a time series. ACF measures correlation between observations at different lags. PACF measures correlation after removing effects of intermediate lags. Returns values for lags 0 to lag_max with 95% confidence bounds. For model fitting, use ts_arima_fit directly instead of computing ACF first.

parameters.description: Request for autocorrelation function (ACF).

column.description: Name of the numeric time series column.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

lag_max.description: Maximum lag to compute. Default: min(10*log10(n), n-1).

function.name: ts_vecm
function.description: Run VECM using Johansen Maximum Likelihood. For cointegrated I(1) time series. Returns cointegration vectors (beta), adjustment speeds (alpha), and eigenvalues.

parameters.description: Request for VECM (Vector Error Correction Model).

columns.description: Names of the columns to include in the VECM model. Should be I(1) cointegrated series.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

lags.description: Number of lags for the VECM (must be at least 2).

function.name: regression_ridge
function.description: Run ridge regression (L2-penalized linear regression). Shortcut for glmnet with alpha=0. Useful when predictors are highly correlated.

parameters.description: Request for ridge regression (shortcut for glmnet with alpha=0).

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

x.description: Names of the independent variable (X) columns.

y.description: Name of the dependent variable (Y) column.

function.name: ml_random_forest
function.description: Run Random Forest regression. Ensemble of decision trees for robust predictions. Returns feature importances, out-of-bag score, and predictions.

parameters.description: Request for Random Forest regression.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

features.description: Names of the feature columns (X variables).

max_depth.description: Maximum depth of each tree. Default is 10.

min_samples_split.description: Minimum samples required to split a node. Default is 2.

target.description: Name of the target column (Y variable).

function.name: regression_smooth_spline
function.description: Fit a smoothing spline to data. Smoothing splines balance goodness-of-fit against smoothness using a penalty on curvature. The smoothing parameter (spar) or degrees of freedom (df) controls the tradeoff. If neither is specified, uses generalized cross-validation (GCV) to automatically select optimal smoothing. Returns fitted values, effective degrees of freedom, and GCV score.

parameters.description: Request for smooth spline fitting.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

x.description: Name of the x (independent) column.

xout.description: Optional points at which to evaluate the fitted spline. If omitted, returns fit at data points.

y.description: Name of the y (dependent) column.

function.name: treatment_entropy_balance
function.description: Compute entropy balancing weights (Hainmueller 2012). Reweights the control group to achieve exact mean balance on specified covariates with the treated group. Minimizes entropy (KL divergence) from uniform weights subject to balance constraints. Useful when exact balance is needed for bias reduction. Returns weights, balance table, and effective sample size.

parameters.description: Request for entropy balancing.

function.name: timeseries_lag
function.description: Shift a time series by k positions. Positive k shifts values backward (lag), negative k shifts forward (lead). Returns the lagged series with NA padding.

parameters.description: Request for time series lag operation.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

function.name: ml_shap_values
function.description: SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) computes feature importance for individual predictions using game-theoretic Shapley values. For tree-based models, uses TreeSHAP (Lundberg et al. 2018) for exact O(TLD^2) computation. Returns: SHAP values matrix (n_obs x n_features), global feature importance (mean |SHAP|), and summary statistics. Each SHAP value represents the contribution of a feature to the difference between the actual prediction and the average prediction. Implements R's 'fastshap' and Python's 'shap' packages.

parameters.description: Request for computing SHAP values.

compute_summary.description: Whether to compute global feature importance summary. Default is true.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

features.description: Names of the feature columns (X variables).

max_obs.description: Maximum observations to compute SHAP values for. Default is all observations.

n_samples.description: Number of background samples for SHAP approximation. If not specified, uses TreeSHAP exact computation.

n_trees.description: Number of trees in the Random Forest. Default is 50.

seed.description: Optional random seed for reproducible results.

target.description: Name of the target column (Y variable).

function.name: ml_bart_causal
function.description: BART Causal estimates heterogeneous treatment effects using Bayesian Additive Regression Trees methodology. Fits separate response surfaces for treated and control groups, then computes CATE = E[Y|T=1,X] - E[Y|T=0,X]. Uses bootstrap for uncertainty quantification. Returns: ATE with confidence interval, CATE estimates for each unit, variable importance for treatment effect heterogeneity. Simplified frequentist approximation to R's bartCause package.

parameters.description: Request for BART-based Causal Inference (bartCause style).

covariates.description: Names of the covariate columns (X variables).

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

outcome.description: Name of the outcome variable (Y).

seed.description: Optional random seed for reproducible results.

treatment.description: Name of the binary treatment variable (W). Must be 0/1.

function.name: db_duckdb_query
function.description: Execute a SQL query against a DuckDB database and load the results as a dataset. DuckDB supports advanced analytics SQL including window functions, CTEs, and more.

function.description: Compute Tukey's five-number summary: minimum, lower-hinge (Q1), median, upper-hinge (Q3), and maximum. Equivalent to R's fivenum().

function.description: Compute balancing weights for causal inference using WeightIt. function.description: Test for autocorrelation in a time series using Box-Pierce or Ljung-Box test. Tests H₀: no autocorrelation up to specified lag. function.name: hypothesis_pairwise_wilcox

factor.description: Name of the grouping factor column (can be string or numeric).

p_adjust_method.description: Method for adjusting p-values: 'holm' (default), 'bonferroni', 'hochberg', 'hommel', 'BH' (Benjamini-Hochberg FDR), 'BY', or 'none'.

response.description: Name of the numeric response variable column.

function.name: hypothesis_quade
function.description: Run Quade test for unreplicated blocked data. Similar to Friedman test but uses weighted rankings based on block ranges, making it more powerful when block effects vary. parameters.description: Request for Quade test.

block.description: Name of the column containing block/subject identifiers.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

treatment.description: Name of the column containing treatment/group labels.

value.description: Name of the numeric column containing the measured values.

function.name: hypothesis_fisher_exact
function.description: Run Fisher's exact test for a 2×2 contingency table. Tests independence between two binary categorical variables using exact probability calculations (hypergeometric distribution). More accurate than chi-squared test for small samples. Returns p-value, odds ratio, and optionally a confidence interval. Use when expected cell counts are small (<5) or when exact p-values are needed.

parameters.description: Request for Fisher's exact test.

col_var.description: Name of the column for columns of the 2×2 table. Must have exactly 2 unique values.

conf_level.description: Confidence level for odds ratio confidence interval (e.g., 0.95). If omitted, CI is not computed.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

row_var.description: Name of the column for rows of the 2×2 table. Must have exactly 2 unique values.

function.name: munge_concat
function.description: Concatenate (row-bind) multiple datasets vertically. All datasets must have the same columns.

datasets.description: List of dataset names to concatenate vertically (row-bind).

result_name.description: Optional name for the concatenated result.

function.description: Create a dataset directly from CSV content provided as a string. Useful for creating small datasets without file I/O.

function.name: competing_risks
function.description: Run Competing Risks analysis using the Aalen-Johansen estimator. Computes cumulative incidence functions (CIF) for multiple event types in the presence of competing risks. confidence_level.description: Confidence level for cumulative incidence estimates. Default is 0.95.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

function.name: generate_random_data
function.description: Generate a random dataset with specified columns and distributions. name.description: Name to assign to the generated dataset. Defaults to 'generated'.

seed.description: Optional random seed for reproducible results.

function.description: Run Tukey's HSD post-hoc test after one-way ANOVA to perform pairwise comparisons between all group means. response.description: Name of the response (dependent) variable column. Must be numeric.

function.name: tool_info
function.description: Get detailed information about a specific tool including its full description, parameters, related tools, and R equivalent. Use this after search_tools to learn more about a specific tool before using it.

parameters.description: Request for getting detailed tool information.

function.name: logit
function.description: Run Logit (logistic) regression for binary outcomes. Uses MLE with Newton-Raphson. Dependent variable must be 0/1.

parameters.description: Request for Logit regression.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

x.description: Names of the independent variable (X) columns.

y.description: Name of the dependent variable (Y) column. Must be binary (0/1).

function.name: spatial_panel_gmm
function.description: Run spatial panel data model via Generalized Method of Moments. Uses IV/GMM estimation for spatial lag models and moment conditions for spatial error. More robust to non-normality than ML. Methods: w2sls (fixed effects), g2sls (random effects GLS), b2sls (between), ec2sls (Baltagi's EC2SLS). Equivalent to R's splm::spgm(). Reference: Kapoor, Kelejian & Prucha (2007).

parameters.description: Request for Spatial Panel GMM estimation (spgm).

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset containing panel data.

entity_col.description: Name of the entity/cross-sectional identifier column.

lag.description: If true, includes spatial lag of dependent variable (uses IV/GMM for identification). Default is false.

method.description: GMM estimation method: 'w2sls' (within/fixed effects, default), 'g2sls' (GLS random effects), 'b2sls' (between), or 'ec2sls' (Baltagi EC2SLS).

spatial_error.description: If true, includes spatially correlated error term. Default is true.

time_col.description: Name of the time period identifier column.

weights.description: Name of previously created spatial weights (from spatial_neighbors tool).

x.description: Names of the independent variable (X) columns.

y.description: Name of the dependent variable (Y) column.

function.name: ts_holt_winters
function.description: Fit Holt-Winters exponential smoothing model to a time series with trend and seasonality. Supports both additive (constant seasonal variation) and multiplicative (proportional variation) seasonality. Automatically optimizes smoothing parameters (alpha, beta, gamma) if not provided. Can generate forecasts for future periods. Returns fitted values, residuals, optimized parameters, and seasonal coefficients.

parameters.description: Request for Holt-Winters exponential smoothing.

alpha.description: Smoothing parameter for the level component (0-1). If not specified, will be optimized.

beta.description: Smoothing parameter for the trend component (0-1). If not specified, will be optimized.

column.description: Name of the column containing the time series values.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

gamma.description: Smoothing parameter for the seasonal component (0-1). If not specified, will be optimized.

horizon.description: Number of periods to forecast ahead. If specified, returns forecasts in addition to fitted values.

period.description: Number of observations per seasonal cycle (e.g., 12 for monthly data with yearly seasonality, 4 for quarterly).

seasonal.description: Type of seasonality: 'additive' (default) for constant seasonal variation, 'multiplicative' for proportional variation.

function.name: db_sqlite_tables
function.description: List all tables in a SQLite database.

parameters.description: Request to list tables in a SQLite database.

db_path.description: Path to the SQLite database file.

function.name: hypothesis_mcnemar
function.description: Run McNemar's chi-squared test for paired nominal data. Tests symmetry in a 2x2 contingency table. Commonly used for comparing two classifiers or before/after studies. Only requires the discordant cells (b and c).

parameters.description: Request for McNemar's chi-squared test.

b.description: The count in the upper-right cell (row 1, column 2) of the 2x2 table. Represents discordant pairs where first classifier is positive and second is negative.

c.description: The count in the lower-left cell (row 2, column 1) of the 2x2 table. Represents discordant pairs where first classifier is negative and second is positive.

correct.description: If true (default), apply Yates' continuity correction. Set to false for the uncorrected version.

function.name: stats_cov_wt
function.description: Compute the weighted covariance matrix for a set of numeric columns. Can use unbiased (reliability) or ML weighting. Equivalent to R's cov.wt().

parameters.description: Request for weighted covariance matrix.

center.description: Whether to center the data (subtract weighted mean). Default is true.

columns.description: Names of the numeric columns to include in the covariance matrix.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

function.name: regression_resettest
function.description: Ramsey's RESET test for functional form misspecification. Tests whether nonlinear terms (powers of fitted values) should be added to the model. Significant result suggests the linear model is misspecified and nonlinear terms may be needed.

parameters.description: Request for Ramsey's RESET test for functional form.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

powers.description: Powers to use for augmentation. Default: [2, 3] tests for quadratic and cubic terms.

reset_type.description: Type of augmentation: 'fitted' (powers of fitted values, default), 'regressor' (powers of regressors), or 'princomp' (powers of first principal component).

x.description: Names of the independent variable (X) columns.

y.description: Name of the dependent variable (Y) column.

function.name: get_seed
function.description: Get the current global random seed setting and list which ML tools support seeded reproducibility.

parameters.description: Request to get the current global seed.

function.name: regression_hac
function.description: Compute HAC (Heteroskedasticity and Autocorrelation Consistent) standard errors using the Newey-West estimator. Essential for time series regression where errors may be both heteroskedastic and autocorrelated. Supports multiple kernel functions and automatic bandwidth selection.

parameters.description: Request for HAC (Newey-West) standard errors.

bandwidth.description: Number of lags for HAC estimation. If not provided, uses automatic Newey-West bandwidth: floor(4 * (n/100)^(2/9)).

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

kernel.description: Kernel function for weighting lags: 'bartlett' (Newey-West, default), 'parzen', 'qs' (quadratic spectral), 'truncated', or 'tukey-hanning'.

prewhiten.description: Apply VAR(1) prewhitening before HAC estimation. Default: false.

x.description: Names of the independent variable (X) columns.

y.description: Name of the dependent variable (Y) column.

function.name: treatment_sbw
function.description: Compute Stable Balancing Weights (SBW) using quadratic programming (Zubizarreta 2015). Directly optimizes for covariate balance rather than modeling the propensity score. Finds weights that minimize variance while achieving exact or approximate balance on covariate means. Advantages: directly targets balance (not propensity score fit), provides stable weights with lower variance than IPW, handles approximate balance when exact is infeasible. Returns weights, balance diagnostics before/after, effective sample size, and optimization details.

parameters.description: Request for stable balancing weights (SBW).

balance_penalty.description: Penalty parameter for approximate balance. Higher values enforce stricter balance. Default is 1000.

balance_tol.description: Tolerance for approximate balance. 0 means exact balance (default), positive values allow some deviation.

covariates.description: Names of covariate columns to balance between treatment groups.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

estimand.description: Target estimand: 'att' (effect on treated, default), 'ate' (average treatment effect), 'atc' (effect on control).

min_weight.description: Minimum weight allowed. Default is 0 (non-negativity constraint).

treatment.description: Column indicating treatment status (1 = treated, 0 = control). Must be binary.

function.name: viz_boxplot
function.description: Generate a box plot visualization comparing the distributions of one or more numeric columns. Shows median, quartiles, and outliers. Returns a base64-encoded PNG image.

parameters.description: Request to generate a box plot.

columns.description: Names of numeric columns to create box plots for.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

function.name: mlogit
function.description: Run McFadden's conditional logit (mlogit) for discrete choice analysis. ind_specific.description: Individual-specific variables that are constant across alternatives (e.g., 'income', 'age'). These get alternative-specific coefficients (different gamma_j for each alternative vs reference).

reference.description: Reference alternative for identification. Default: first alternative (alphabetically).

function.name: anova_two_way
function.description: Run two-way Analysis of Variance (ANOVA) to test effects of two factors and their interaction on a response variable. Returns F-statistics and p-values for each factor and the interaction term. Use for factorial experimental designs.

parameters.description: Request for two-way ANOVA.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

response.description: Name of the response (dependent) variable column. Must be numeric.

function.description: Run Hausman specification test to choose between Fixed Effects and Random Effects. Tests H0: RE is consistent. If p-value < 0.05, use Fixed Effects.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

function.description: Run Difference-in-Differences (DiD) estimation. Estimates causal treatment effects by comparing treated vs control groups before and after treatment. For staggered treatment adoption across multiple periods, use staggered_did instead.

function.description: Run regularized regression with elastic net penalty (glmnet). Combines L1 (lasso) and L2 (ridge) penalties. Set alpha=1 for lasso, alpha=0 for ridge, or 0<alpha<1 for elastic net. Returns coefficient path along lambda sequence.

parameters.description: Request for glmnet (elastic net, lasso, ridge) regression.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

family.description: Model family: 'gaussian' (default) for linear regression, 'binomial' for logistic regression.

lambda.description: Optional sequence of lambda (regularization) values. If omitted, automatically generates a path.

standardize.description: Whether to standardize predictors before fitting. Default is true.

x.description: Names of the independent variable (X) columns.

y.description: Name of the dependent variable (Y) column.

function.name: str_replace_value
function.description: Replace exact values in a column with a new value. Use to clean sentinel values like -99, 'N/A', or 'missing' by replacing them (use null as new_value to convert to missing). For pattern-based replacement, use str_regex_replace. Call this directly — do NOT call head_dataset or describe_dataset first.

parameters.description: Request to replace exact values in a column.

function.description: Split a string column by a pattern (supports regex) into multiple columns named prefix_0, prefix_1, etc.

function.name: timeseries_spectrum
function.description: Estimate spectral density (power spectrum) of a time series. Returns spectral density at Fourier frequencies showing how variance is distributed across frequency components. column.description: Name of the column containing the time series values.

d.description: Number of differences to make the series stationary.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

function.description: Perform MSTL (Multiple Seasonal-Trend decomposition using LOESS) on a time series. Extracts trend, seasonal components, and residuals.

column.description: Name of the column containing the time series values.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

periods.description: Seasonal periods to extract (e.g., [7, 365] for daily data with weekly and yearly seasonality).

function.name: power_prop_test
function.description: Compute power or sample size for two-sample proportion tests. Given 4 of {n, p1, p2, sig_level, power}, computes the 5th. Use for study design comparing proportions between two groups.

parameters.description: Request for power analysis of proportion test.

n.description: Sample size per group. Leave None to solve for required sample size.

sig_level.description: Significance level (Type I error rate). Default: 0.05.

function.name: hypothesis_chisq_gof
function.description: Run Pearson's chi-squared goodness-of-fit test to check if observed category frequencies match expected probabilities. Tests H₀: observed frequencies follow the expected distribution. Returns chi-squared statistic, p-value, degrees of freedom, and residuals. parameters.description: Request for chi-squared goodness-of-fit test.

column.description: Name of the categorical column. Counts of each unique value will be tested.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

probs.description: Expected probabilities for each category. Must sum to 1.0. If omitted, uniform distribution is assumed.

function.name: ml_svm
function.description: Run Linear Support Vector Machine (SVM) for binary classification. Uses SMO algorithm. Returns weights, bias, support vector count, and predictions.
