dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

features.description: Names of the feature columns (X variables).

max_iterations.description: Maximum number of iterations. Default is 1000.

target.description: Name of the binary target column (Y variable). Must have exactly 2 unique values.

function.name: regression_ols
function.description: Run Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) regression. Returns coefficients, standard errors, t-values, p-values, R-squared, and F-statistic. For comparing group means with a single categorical predictor, consider anova_one_way instead.

parameters.description: Request for OLS regression.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

x.description: Names of the independent variable (X) columns.

y.description: Name of the dependent variable (Y) column.

function.name: stats_model_tables
function.description: Compute cell means or effects tables from one-way or two-way ANOVA. Returns group means or deviations from grand mean with optional standard errors. Equivalent to R's model.tables().

parameters.description: Request for model tables from ANOVA.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

factors.description: Name of the factor column for one-way ANOVA, or list of two factor columns for two-way ANOVA.

response.description: Name of the response column (Y variable).

se.description: Whether to compute standard errors. Default is true.

table_type.description: Type of table: 'means' (default) or 'effects' (deviations from grand mean).

function.name: viz_dendrogram
function.description: Generate a dendrogram (tree diagram) from hierarchical clustering results. Shows how clusters are merged at each level with merge distances. Takes a linkage matrix from hierarchical clustering output.

parameters.description: Request to visualize hierarchical clustering results as a dendrogram.

height.description: Height of the chart in pixels (default: 600).

labels.description: Optional labels for leaf nodes (original samples). If not provided, uses indices.

linkage_matrix.description: Linkage matrix from hierarchical clustering. Array of [cluster1, cluster2, distance, size] tuples.

width.description: Width of the chart in pixels (default: 800).

function.name: str_to_uppercase
function.description: Convert all characters in a string column to uppercase.

parameters.description: Request to convert a string column to uppercase.

column.description: Name of the string column to convert to uppercase.

dataset.description: Name or ID of the dataset.

function.name: set_seed
function.description: Set a global random seed for ML operations (kmeans, random_forest, tsne). When set, ML tools will use this seed as a fallback if no per-tool seed is specified. Clear by calling with no seed value.

parameters.description: Request to set the global random seed for ML reproducibility.

seed.description: The random seed value. Set to null/omit to clear the global seed.

function.name: ml_ctree
function.description: Conditional Inference Trees (ctree) - decision trees with unbiased variable selection via permutation tests. Based on Hothorn, Hornik & Zeileis (2006). Unlike CART, ctree uses statistical significance tests for variable selection, avoiding bias towards variables with many possible split points. The tree grows until no significant relationship exists between predictors and response (no pruning needed). Equivalent to R's partykit::ctree.

parameters.description: Request for Conditional Inference Trees (ctree).

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

features.description: Names of the feature columns (X variables).

maxdepth.description: Maximum depth of the tree. 0 means unlimited. Default is 0.

minbucket.description: Minimum number of observations in a terminal node. Default is 7.

mincriterion.description: Value of 1 - p-value that must be exceeded to implement a split. Default is 0.95 (p < 0.05).

minsplit.description: Minimum number of observations in a node required to attempt a split. Default is 20.

seed.description: Optional random seed for reproducible results.

target.description: Name of the target column (Y variable). Can be numeric (regression) or categorical (classification).

teststat.description: Type of test statistic: 'quadratic' (chi-squared) or 'max' (maximum). Default is 'quadratic'.

testtype.description: P-value adjustment method: 'bonferroni', 'univariate', or 'none'. Default is 'bonferroni'.

function.name: feglm
function.description: Run Generalized Linear Model with high-dimensional fixed effects (FEGLM). Supports Logit, Probit, Poisson, and Gaussian families with multiple absorbed fixed effects. Uses IRLS + Method of Alternating Projections. Equivalent to R's alpaca::feglm().

parameters.description: Request for Generalized Linear Model with High-Dimensional Fixed Effects (FEGLM).

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

family.description: GLM family: 'logit' (binomial logit, default), 'probit' (binomial probit), 'poisson' (count data), or 'gaussian' (continuous, equivalent to linear HDFE).

fe.description: Column names for fixed effects to absorb (e.g., ['firm_id', 'year']). Supports multiple dimensions.

max_iter.description: Maximum IRLS iterations for estimation. Default is 25.

tolerance.description: Convergence tolerance for coefficient changes. Default is 1e-8.

x.description: Names of the independent variable (X) columns.

y.description: Name of the dependent variable (Y) column. For logit/probit must be binary (0/1). For Poisson must be non-negative counts.

function.name: timeseries_arma_to_ma
function.description: Convert ARMA model to its infinite MA representation (psi weights). The psi weights show the impulse response function of the model.

parameters.description: Request for ARMA to MA conversion.

lag_max.description: Number of MA (psi) weights to compute. Default is 10.

function.name: ts_varma
function.description: Run VARMA(p,q) model using Hannan-Rissanen estimation. Combines autoregressive and moving average components for multivariate time series.

parameters.description: Request for VARMA (Vector ARMA) model.

columns.description: Names of the columns to include in the VARMA model.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

function.name: multivariate_factanal
function.description: Run Maximum Likelihood Factor Analysis to identify latent factors underlying observed variables. Models correlation structure as x = Λf + e where Λ is the loadings matrix, f are factor scores, and e is error. Returns loadings matrix, uniquenesses (specific variances), communalities (variance explained per variable), variance proportions, chi-squared goodness-of-fit test, and optionally factor scores. Supports varimax (orthogonal) and promax (oblique) rotation.

parameters.description: Request for factor analysis.

columns.description: Names of the numeric columns to include in factor analysis. Should have at least n_factors + 1 variables.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

n_factors.description: Number of factors to extract. Must be between 1 and (number of variables - 1). Rule of thumb: fewer factors that explain most variance.

rotation.description: Factor rotation method: 'varimax' (default, orthogonal), 'promax' (oblique, allows correlated factors), or 'none'.

scores.description: Method for computing factor scores: 'none' (default), 'regression' (Thomson's method), or 'bartlett' (weighted least squares).

function.name: panel_pvcm
function.description: Run Variable Coefficients Model (PVCM) for heterogeneous panel data. Allows slope coefficients to vary across entities. Two modes: 'within' runs separate OLS per entity, 'random' (Swamy 1970) computes a GLS weighted average. Also computes homogeneity test for coefficient equality.

parameters.description: Request for Variable Coefficients Model (PVCM).

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded panel dataset.

model.description: Model type: 'within' for separate OLS per entity (default), 'random' for Swamy (1970) GLS estimator.

x.description: Names of the independent variable (X) columns.

y.description: Name of the dependent variable (Y) column.

function.name: timeseries_diffinv
function.description: Compute the inverse of differencing (cumulative sum). Reconstructs the original series from differences given initial values.

parameters.description: Request for inverse differencing.

column.description: Name of the column containing differenced values.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

differences.description: Number of times differencing was applied. Default is 1.

xi.description: Initial values to start the cumulative sum.

function.name: anova_manova
function.description: Run Multivariate Analysis of Variance (MANOVA) to test whether group means differ across multiple response variables simultaneously. Returns four test statistics: Wilks' Lambda (most popular), Pillai's Trace (most robust, default), Hotelling-Lawley Trace, and Roy's Largest Root. Each with approximate F-statistic and p-value. Use when you have 2+ continuous response variables and want to test group differences while accounting for correlations between responses.

parameters.description: Request for MANOVA (Multivariate Analysis of Variance).

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

factor.description: Name of the factor (grouping) variable column. Groups observations for comparison.

response_vars.description: Names of the response (dependent) variable columns. Must be numeric. MANOVA requires at least 2 response variables.

test.description: Test statistic to use: 'pillai' (default, most robust), 'wilks' (most popular), 'hotelling' (Hotelling-Lawley), or 'roy' (Roy's largest root). All four are always computed.

function.name: compute_correlation
function.description: Compute the Pearson correlation matrix for all numeric columns in a dataset.

parameters.description: Request for correlation matrix.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

function.name: evalue
function.description: Compute E-values for sensitivity analysis to unmeasured confounding (VanderWeele & Ding 2017). The E-value is the minimum strength of association that an unmeasured confounder would need with both treatment and outcome to fully explain away an observed effect. Supports risk ratios (RR), odds ratios (OR), hazard ratios (HR), standardized mean differences (SMD), and risk differences (RD). A large E-value means considerable confounding would be needed to explain away the effect. Returns E-value for point estimate and confidence interval limit closest to null.

parameters.description: Request for E-value sensitivity analysis for unmeasured confounding.

baseline_risk.description: Baseline risk (probability in unexposed group), required for risk difference. Must be between 0 and 1.

ci_lower.description: Lower bound of the 95% confidence interval. Optional but recommended.

ci_upper.description: Upper bound of the 95% confidence interval. Optional but recommended.

effect_type.description: Type of effect measure: 'rr' (risk ratio), 'or' (odds ratio), 'hr' (hazard ratio), 'smd' (standardized mean difference), 'rd' (risk difference).

point.description: Point estimate of the effect measure (e.g., RR=2.5, OR=3.0, SMD=0.5).

rare.description: Whether the outcome is rare (<15% prevalence). If true, OR/HR used as RR approximation. If false, sqrt transformation applied. Default: true for OR/HR.

se.description: Standard error of the estimate. Required for SMD if CI not provided.

function.name: munge_sort
function.description: Sort a dataset by one or more columns in ascending or descending order.

parameters.description: Request to sort a dataset.

by.description: List of column names to sort by.

dataset.description: Name or ID of the dataset.

descending.description: If true, sort in descending order. Default is ascending.

result_name.description: Optional name for the result. If not provided, overwrites the source dataset.

function.name: cleaning_session_start
function.description: Start a new cleaning session for a dataset. Returns a session ID that can be used to track progress, apply operations, and rollback changes. Each session maintains checkpoints for undo capability.

parameters.description: Request to start a new cleaning session.

dataset.description: Name or ID of the dataset to create a cleaning session for.

session_name.description: Optional descriptive name for the cleaning session.

function.name: stats_iqr
function.description: Compute the interquartile range (Q3 - Q1) of a numeric column. Supports different quantile types (1-9). Equivalent to R's IQR().

parameters.description: Request for interquartile range.

column.description: Name of the numeric column.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

qtype.description: Quantile type (1-9). Type 7 (default) matches R's default.

function.name: munge_mutate
function.description: Create a new column by applying arithmetic operations or functions. Supports: arithmetic (+, -, *, /), functions (log, exp, sqrt, abs, square), or constant values.

parameters.description: Request to create a new column by computation.

dataset.description: Name or ID of the dataset.

expr_type.description: Expression type: 'arithmetic' (e.g., col1 + col2), 'function' (e.g., log(col)), or 'constant'.

left.description: Left operand: column name for arithmetic, column for function, or constant value.

operator.description: Operator for arithmetic: '+', '-', '*', '/'. For function: function name ('log', 'exp', 'sqrt', 'abs', 'square').

right.description: Right operand: column name for arithmetic expressions.

function.name: zeroinfl
function.description: Run zero-inflated Poisson or negative binomial regression for count data with excess zeros. Models both the zero-inflation probability and the count process. Equivalent to R's pscl::zeroinfl().

parameters.description: Request for zero-inflated models.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

x.description: Names of the independent variable (X) columns for the count model.

y.description: Name of the count dependent variable (Y) column.

z.description: Names of the variables for the zero-inflation model. If not specified, uses intercept only.

function.name: ordered_model
function.description: Run ordered logit or probit regression (proportional odds model) for ordered categorical outcomes. Estimates threshold (cut-point) parameters. Equivalent to R's MASS::polr().

parameters.description: Request for ordered logit/probit regression.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

x.description: Names of the independent variable (X) columns.

y.description: Name of the ordered categorical dependent variable (Y) column.

function.name: ml_dbscan
function.description: Run DBSCAN (Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise) clustering. Finds clusters of arbitrary shape and identifies outliers as noise points. Does not require specifying number of clusters.

parameters.description: Request for DBSCAN clustering.

columns.description: Names of the numeric columns to use as features for clustering.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

eps.description: Maximum distance between two samples for them to be considered in the same neighborhood.

min_samples.description: Minimum number of samples in a neighborhood for a point to be considered a core point.

function.name: ts_garch_fit
function.description: Fit a GARCH(p,q) model for time-varying volatility. Estimates the conditional variance equation: σ²_t = ω + Σα_i ε²_{t-i} + Σβ_j σ²_{t-j}. Reports persistence, unconditional variance, and half-life of volatility shocks.

parameters.description: Request for GARCH model fitting (volatility modeling).

column.description: Name of the column containing returns (e.g., stock returns, percentage changes).

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

include_mean.description: Whether to include a mean term in the model. Default: true.

p.description: Number of ARCH (lagged squared residual) terms. Default: 1.

q.description: Number of GARCH (lagged variance) terms. Default: 1.

function.name: panel_hdfe
function.description: Run High-Dimensional Fixed Effects (HDFE) regression with multiple absorbed fixed effects (e.g., firm + year + industry). Uses the Method of Alternating Projections (MAP) for efficient estimation. Equivalent to R's lfe::felm() or Stata's reghdfe.

parameters.description: Request for High-Dimensional Fixed Effects (HDFE).

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

fe.description: Column names for fixed effects to absorb (e.g., ['firm_id', 'year']). Supports multiple dimensions.

max_iterations.description: Maximum iterations for MAP algorithm. Default is 10000.

tolerance.description: Convergence tolerance for the Method of Alternating Projections. Default is 1e-8.

x.description: Names of the independent variable (X) columns.

y.description: Name of the dependent variable (Y) column.

function.name: treatment_tmle
function.description: Estimate Average Treatment Effect (ATE) using TMLE - a doubly robust, semiparametric efficient estimator. TMLE uses a targeting step to optimize the bias-variance tradeoff for the ATE. More efficient than standard AIPW due to the fluctuation model. Returns ATE estimate with influence curve-based standard errors and confidence intervals.

parameters.description: Request for Targeted Maximum Likelihood Estimation (TMLE).

covariates.description: Names of covariate columns to include in both propensity score and outcome models.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

outcome.description: Name of the outcome variable column. Can be binary or continuous.

ps_lower.description: Lower bound for propensity score truncation. Default is 0.01.

ps_upper.description: Upper bound for propensity score truncation. Default is 0.99.

q_model.description: Outcome model type: 'logistic' for binary outcomes (default), 'linear' for continuous outcomes.

treatment.description: Column indicating treatment status (1 = treated, 0 = control). Must be binary.

function.name: treatment_ipw
function.description: Estimate Average Treatment Effect (ATE) or Average Treatment Effect on Treated (ATT) using Inverse Probability Weighting. Uses propensity scores to create pseudo-populations that balance covariates between treatment groups. Returns effect estimate with bootstrap standard errors and confidence intervals. Returns a point estimate (ATE/ATT). For matched samples with balance diagnostics, use propensity_matching instead.

parameters.description: Request for Inverse Probability Weighting (IPW) treatment effect estimation.

bootstrap.description: Number of bootstrap replications for standard error estimation. Default is 999.

covariates.description: Names of covariate columns to include in propensity score model.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

estimand.description: Treatment effect estimand: 'ate' for Average Treatment Effect (default), 'att' for Average Treatment Effect on Treated.

outcome.description: Name of the outcome variable column.

treatment.description: Column indicating treatment status (1 = treated, 0 = control). Must be binary.

trim.description: Trim observations with propensity scores below trim or above 1-trim. Default is 0.05.

function.name: causal_impact_analysis
function.description: Estimate the causal effect of an intervention using Bayesian Structural Time Series (BSTS). Uses pre-intervention data to build a counterfactual prediction, then compares with observed post-intervention data to estimate the causal effect. Optionally uses control time series that are correlated with the response but unaffected by the intervention. Returns cumulative/average effects with credible intervals and Bayesian p-value.

parameters.description: Request for CausalImpact analysis (Bayesian Structural Time Series for causal inference).

alpha.description: Significance level for credible intervals. Default: 0.05 (95% credible intervals).

control_cols.description: Optional names of columns to use as control time series. These should be correlated with the response but unaffected by the intervention.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

include_trend.description: Whether to include a trend component in the model. Default: false.

post_period_end.description: End time value of the post-intervention period (inclusive).

post_period_start.description: Start time value of the post-intervention period (inclusive). This is when the intervention occurs.

pre_period_end.description: End time value of the pre-intervention period (inclusive).

pre_period_start.description: Start time value of the pre-intervention period (inclusive). This is the period used to train the model.

response_col.description: Name of the column containing the response variable to analyze.

seasonal_period.description: If the data has seasonality, specify the period (e.g., 12 for monthly data with yearly seasonality).

function.name: rd_fuzzy
function.description: Run Fuzzy Regression Discontinuity estimation. For cases where treatment probability (not assignment) jumps at the cutoff. Uses a Wald estimator (ratio of reduced-form to first-stage). Returns Local Average Treatment Effect (LATE).

cutoff.description: Cutoff value for the running variable. Default is 0.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

h.description: Main bandwidth h. If not specified, uses automatic selection.

level.description: Confidence level for intervals. Default is 0.95.

outcome.description: Name of the outcome variable (Y) column.

p.description: Polynomial order for estimation. Default is 1.

running_var.description: Name of the running (forcing) variable (X) column.

treatment.description: Name of the treatment indicator column (actual treatment received, 0/1).

function.name: bacon_decomp
function.description: Decompose a two-way fixed effects (TWFE) DiD estimate into weighted 2x2 comparisons using Goodman-Bacon (2021) decomposition. Reveals which comparisons (treated vs. never-treated, treated vs. not-yet-treated, later vs. earlier treated) contribute to the overall estimate and with what weights. Essential for understanding potential biases from 'forbidden' comparisons when treatment effects are heterogeneous over time.

parameters.description: Request for Goodman-Bacon decomposition of staggered DiD.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded panel dataset with staggered treatment.

outcome.description: Name of the outcome variable column.

time_col.description: Column containing the time period identifier (e.g., year, quarter).

treatment_col.description: Binary treatment indicator column (0 = untreated, 1 = treated). Should be 0 before treatment and 1 after for each unit.

unit_col.description: Column containing the unit/individual identifier (e.g., state_id, firm_id).

function.name: sem_model
function.description: Run Spatial Error Model (SEM): y = Xβ + u, where u = λWu + ε. Estimates spatial error parameter λ via maximum likelihood. Use when spatial dependence is in the error term (nuisance dependence, e.g., omitted spatially correlated variables). Equivalent to R's spatialreg::errorsarlm().

parameters.description: Request for Spatial Error Model (SEM).

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

weights.description: Name of previously created spatial weights (from spatial_neighbors tool).

x.description: Names of the independent variable (X) columns.

y.description: Name of the dependent variable (Y) column.

function.name: ts_changepoint
function.description: Detect changepoints (structural breaks) in a time series using PELT or Binary Segmentation. parameters.description: Request for changepoint detection.

change_type.description: Type of change to detect: 'mean' (default), 'variance', or 'both'.

column.description: Name of the column containing the time series values.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

method.description: Algorithm to use: 'pelt' (Pruned Exact Linear Time, default) or 'binary' (Binary Segmentation).

min_segment_length.description: Minimum number of observations between changepoints. Default is 2.

penalty.description: Penalty for adding a changepoint. Higher values = fewer changepoints. Default uses BIC (log(n)).

function.name: regression_line
function.description: Tukey's resistant line - robust regression using medians instead of means, making it resistant to outliers. Divides data into three groups and uses group medians to determine slope and intercept. Returns coefficients, fitted values, and residuals.

parameters.description: Request for Tukey's resistant line.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

iter.description: Number of polishing iterations. Default is 1.

x.description: Name of the predictor column (X variable).

y.description: Name of the response column (Y variable).

function.name: head_dataset
function.description: Preview the first N rows of a loaded dataset (default: 5 rows). Returns data in a formatted table.

parameters.description: Request to preview rows from a dataset.

n.description: Number of rows to return. Default is 5.

function.description: Test for trend in proportions across ordered groups (Cochran-Armitage test). Tests whether proportions increase or decrease linearly with group scores. Commonly used in dose-response studies. Returns chi-squared statistic with 1 df and p-value.

scores.description: Optional scores for each group. If omitted, uses 1, 2, 3, ... (equally spaced).

successes.description: Name of column containing number of successes in each group.

trials.description: Name of column containing number of trials in each group.

function.name: ml_ppr
function.description: Projection Pursuit Regression (PPR) - a dimension reduction regression that fits models of the form y = sum(f_k(alpha_k' * x)). Finds optimal projection directions and ridge functions. Returns projection directions, coefficients, fitted values, and goodness-of-fit metrics. Useful for non-linear regression when relationships are complex.

parameters.description: Request for Projection Pursuit Regression (PPR).

bass.description: Bass parameter for supsmu smoothing (0-10). Higher = smoother. Default is 0.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

features.description: Names of the feature columns (X variables).

max_terms.description: Maximum terms to consider during forward selection. Default is nterms.

sm_method.description: Smoothing method for ridge functions: 'supsmu' (default), 'spline', or 'gcvspline'.

target.description: Name of the target column (Y variable).

function.name: munge_one_hot_encode
function.description: One-hot encode a categorical column, creating binary indicator columns for each category. Use drop_first=true to avoid multicollinearity in regression.

parameters.description: Request to one-hot encode a categorical column.

column.description: Categorical column name to one-hot encode.

dataset.description: Name or ID of the dataset.

drop_first.description: If true, drop first category to avoid multicollinearity. Default is false.

function.name: multivariate_cancor
function.description: Run Canonical Correlation Analysis (CCA) to find linear combinations of two sets of variables that have maximum correlation with each other. Returns canonical correlations (in decreasing order), coefficients for X variables (xcoef), and coefficients for Y variables (ycoef). The canonical variates are X*xcoef and Y*ycoef. function.name: staggered_did

function.name: hypothesis_wilcoxon
function.description: Run Wilcoxon non-parametric test for location. function.name: sar_probit_model
function.description: Run Spatial Autoregressive (SAR) Probit model for binary dependent variables: y* = rho*W*y* + X*beta + epsilon, y = 1(y* > 0). seed.description: Random seed for reproducibility. Optional.

weights.description: Name of previously created spatial weights (from spatial_neighbors tool).

x.description: Names of the independent variable (X) columns.

y.description: Name of the binary dependent variable (Y) column (0/1 values).

function.name: munge_filter
function.description: Filter rows in a dataset based on a column condition. Supports operators: 'eq', 'ne', 'gt', 'ge', 'lt', 'le', 'contains', 'starts_with', 'ends_with'. The value is parsed based on the column type.

function.name: cox_ph
function.description: Run Cox Proportional Hazards (Cox PH) regression model. Semi-parametric regression estimating covariate effects on hazard rate without assuming a baseline hazard form. function.name: power_anova_test

function.name: search_tools
function.description: Search for analytics tools by natural language description. Use this when you need to find the right tool for an analysis task. function.name: iv_2sls
function.description: Run Instrumental Variables (2SLS) regression. Use when an explanatory variable is endogenous (correlated with the error term). Requires valid instruments. function.name: ml_causal_forest
function.description: Causal Forest estimates heterogeneous treatment effects (CATE) using random forests adapted for causal inference. dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

function.name: regression_standardization
function.description: Estimate causal effects using regression standardization (G-computation/parametric g-formula). treatment.description: Column indicating treatment status (1 = treated, 0 = control). Must be binary.

function.description: Export the current session including all loaded datasets and their metadata. Can save to file or return as string. Useful for saving your analysis state to resume later.

function.name: gformula
function.description: Estimate causal effects of time-varying treatments using the parametric g-formula (generalized formula). columns.description: List of column names to compare across datasets.

comparison_type.description: Comparison type: 'summary' (side-by-side stats), 'correlation' (correlation differences), or 'distribution' (distribution comparison).

datasets.description: List of dataset names to compare. Each must be previously loaded.

function.name: iv_first_stage
function.description: Run ONLY first-stage diagnostics to test instrument strength. Reports F-statistic (F > 10 suggests strong instruments), R-squared, and coefficient estimates. Note: iv_2sls already includes first-stage results — use this only when you need first-stage diagnostics without the full 2SLS estimation.

parameters.description: Request for first-stage diagnostics.

controls.description: Optional control variables to include in first-stage regression.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

endogenous_var.description: Name of the endogenous variable to test instrument strength for.

function.name: treatment_double_ml
function.description: Estimate causal treatment effects using Double/Debiased Machine Learning. Uses Neyman-orthogonal score functions and K-fold cross-fitting to achieve root-n consistent and asymptotically normal estimates. Supports Partially Linear Regression (PLR: Y = theta*D + g(X) + eps) and Interactive Regression Model (IRM: binary treatment with heterogeneous effects). Returns treatment effect estimate with influence function-based standard errors and diagnostic information.

parameters.description: Request for Double/Debiased Machine Learning (DoubleML) estimation.

covariates.description: Names of covariate columns (X) for nuisance model estimation.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

model_type.description: DML model type: 'plr' for Partially Linear Regression (default, Y = theta*D + g(X) + eps), 'irm' for Interactive Regression Model (binary treatment, heterogeneous effects).

n_folds.description: Number of folds for cross-fitting. Default is 5. Must be at least 2.

outcome.description: Name of the outcome variable column (Y).

seed.description: Random seed for reproducible cross-fitting splits. If omitted, uses random seed.

treatment.description: Name of the treatment variable column (D). Can be continuous or binary.

trim.description: Trim propensity scores to [trim, 1-trim] for IRM model. Default is 0.01.

function.name: regression_cv_glmnet
function.description: Run cross-validated elastic net/lasso/ridge regression to select optimal lambda. Returns lambda.min (minimum CV error) and lambda.1se (most regularized within 1 SE of minimum).

parameters.description: Request for cross-validated glmnet.

alpha.description: Elastic net mixing parameter: 0 for pure ridge, 1 for lasso (default), between 0-1 for elastic net.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

family.description: Model family: 'gaussian' (default) for linear regression, 'binomial' for logistic regression.

nfolds.description: Number of cross-validation folds. Default is 10.

nlambda.description: Number of lambda values in the path. Default is 100.

seed.description: Random seed for fold assignment reproducibility.

standardize.description: Whether to standardize predictors before fitting. Default is true.

x.description: Names of the independent variable (X) columns.

y.description: Name of the dependent variable (Y) column.

function.name: regression_gls
function.description: Fit a Generalized Least Squares (GLS) regression model. GLS extends OLS to handle correlated or heteroscedastic errors. Correlation structures: 'ar1' (autoregressive), 'compound_symmetry' (equal correlation), 'identity' (OLS). For AR(1), rho can be specified or auto-estimated from OLS residuals. Returns coefficients, standard errors, t-values, p-values, and model fit statistics.

parameters.description: Request for GLS (Generalized Least Squares).

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

intercept.description: Whether to include an intercept. Default is true.

rho.description: Correlation parameter rho for AR(1) or compound symmetry. If omitted with 'ar1', auto-estimated from OLS residuals.

x.description: Names of the independent (x) variable columns.

y.description: Name of the dependent (y) variable column.

function.name: preview_cleaning
function.description: Preview a data cleaning operation before applying it. Shows how many rows would be affected, sample changes, and warnings. Supports: trim, lowercase, uppercase, fill_na, drop_na, deduplicate, replace, filter.

parameters.description: Request for previewing a cleaning operation.

columns.description: Column name(s) to apply the operation to. For some operations this can be omitted to apply to all columns.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

filter_value.description: For filter: value to compare against.

how.description: For drop_na: 'any' (drop if any null) or 'all' (drop only if all null).

keep.description: For deduplicate: which duplicate to keep ('first', 'last', 'none').

old_value.description: For replace: the value to search for and replace.

operation.description: The type of cleaning operation: 'trim', 'lowercase', 'uppercase', 'fill_na', 'drop_na', 'deduplicate', 'replace', or 'filter'.

sample_size.description: Number of example changes to include in the preview. Default is 5.

value.description: For fill_na with constant: the fill value. For replace: the new value.

function.name: stats_mad
function.description: Compute the median absolute deviation (MAD), a robust measure of dispersion. By default, scaled by 1.4826 for consistency with the standard deviation of normal distributions. Equivalent to R's mad().

parameters.description: Request for median absolute deviation.

center.description: Center to use. Default is 'median'. Can also use 'mean'.

column.description: Name of the numeric column.

constant.description: Scaling constant. Default 1.4826 makes MAD consistent for normal data.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

function.name: str_substring
function.description: Extract a substring from each string in a column. Supports negative indices to count from end.

parameters.description: Request to extract a substring.

column.description: Name of the string column.

dataset.description: Name or ID of the dataset.

length.description: Number of characters to extract. If not provided, extracts to end.

start.description: Start index (0-based). Negative values count from end.

function.name: db_sqlite_query
function.description: Execute a SQL query against a SQLite database and load the results as a dataset. The resulting dataset can then be analyzed using other tools.

parameters.description: Request to query a SQLite database.

db_path.description: Path to the SQLite database file (.db, .sqlite, .sqlite3).

name.description: Optional name for the resulting dataset. If not provided, a default name will be generated.

query.description: SQL query to execute (SELECT statements only recommended).

function.name: mediation_analysis
function.description: Perform causal mediation analysis to decompose treatment effects into direct and indirect (mediated) effects. Uses IPW-based identification following Huber (2014). Returns Natural Direct Effect (NDE), Natural Indirect Effect (NIE), proportion mediated, and bootstrap inference.

parameters.description: Request for Causal Mediation Analysis.

bootstrap.description: Number of bootstrap replications for standard error estimation. Default is 999.

covariates.description: Names of covariate columns for adjustment in propensity score models.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

mediator.description: Name of the mediator variable column - the intermediate variable through which treatment may affect the outcome.

outcome.description: Name of the outcome variable column.

treatment.description: Column indicating treatment status (1 = treated, 0 = control). Must be binary.

trim.description: Trim observations with propensity scores below trim or above 1-trim. Default is 0.05.

function.name: timeseries_acf_to_ar
function.description: Compute AR coefficients from autocorrelation function using the Yule-Walker equations. Also returns partial autocorrelations.

parameters.description: Request for ACF to AR conversion.

acf.description: Autocorrelation function values starting at lag 1.

function.name: timeseries_decompose
function.description: Decompose a time series into trend, seasonal, and random components using moving averages. Implements R's decompose() function. Supports additive (Y = T + S + R) and multiplicative (Y = T × S × R) decomposition.

parameters.description: Request for classical seasonal decomposition.

column.description: Name of the column containing the time series values.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

decompose_type.description: Type of decomposition: 'additive' (default, Y = Trend + Seasonal + Random) or 'multiplicative' (Y = Trend × Seasonal × Random).

period.description: Number of observations per seasonal cycle (e.g., 12 for monthly data with yearly seasonality, 4 for quarterly).

function.name: regression_clustered
function.description: Run OLS regression with clustered standard errors. Supports one-way (firm, state) or two-way (firm + time) clustering. Essential for panel data with correlated errors.

parameters.description: Request for OLS with clustered standard errors.

cluster1.description: Column name for first clustering dimension (e.g., 'firm_id').

cluster2.description: Optional column for second clustering dimension (e.g., 'year'). If provided, two-way clustering is used.

dataset.description: Name or ID of a previously loaded dataset.

x.description: Names of the independent variable (X) columns.

y.description: Name of the dependent variable (Y) column.

function.name: munge_fill_na
function.description: Fill null values using a strategy: 'mean', 'median', 'mode', 'forward', 'backward', or a constant value.

parameters.description: Request to fill null values.

columns.description: Column names to fill nulls in. If not provided, fills all columns.

dataset.description: Name or ID of the dataset.

strategy.description: Fill strategy: 'mean', 'median', 'mode', 'forward', 'backward', or a constant value.
